title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a known high-traffic event without sufficient battery capacity or contingency planning for the traffic patterns that actually occurred. When Fourth of July celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge created severe congestion, multiple vehicles became stranded as their batteries drained. The system failed because it was used under conditions—massive unplanned road closures and traffic volumes—that exceeded what it was built to handle.

This was a deployment failure at the operational level, not a failure of the autonomous driving technology itself. Waymo could have caught this by modeling battery consumption against historical traffic data for major events, or by restricting service during predicted peak congestion periods. The company's response acknowledged the need to improve "vehicle resilience during major traffic disruptions," suggesting the capability to operate in such conditions was assumed but not verified.

It is not established whether Waymo had received warnings about the traffic impact of the holiday event, or what specific conditions triggered the decision to operate the fleet at normal capacity that day.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge on Saturday. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported.

Following the incident, Waymo stated it would evaluate ways to strengthen vehicle resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the situation with public and private partners to improve future responses. This was not the first issue Waymo faced in San Francisco, as the company had previously paused service in December after a power outage affected over 100,000 customers and caused some traffic lights to malfunction, which also impacted autonomous vehicles at intersections.
